text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said it was recommending shares of Metalcorp Ltd as a buy, reflecting longer-term potential in a growing metal recycling sector.
"Buy for longer term earnings growth in an expanding metal recycling sector with ongoing mergers," Morgan analyst Maree Klemm said in an investment report.
Metalcorp is the second-largest scrap metal recycler in Australia after Simsmetal Ltd and continued to be acquisitive to generate improved economies of scale, Klemm said.
Recent acquisitions of AB Metals and Metal Recyclers gave Metalcorp a national and international profile, Klemm said.

"With structural changes in the steel industry and scrap metal sector, the outlook in metal recycling should improve," Klemm said. "However the immediate prognosis is for depressed metal markets to persist for much of financial 1996/97."
Longer-term, Klemm said she forecast a prolonged period of growth in the metal recycling sector.
Klemm forecast a net profit for Metalcorp in the current year ended June 30, 1997 of A$10.1 million compared with a reported $5.3 million in 1995/96.
"The (current) December half is expected to be difficult with a stronger second half keeping profits at the forecast level for 1996/97," Klemm said.
Scrap metal had experienced a downturn after several buoyant years and while margins were steady, demand and prices in Asia and Australia had weakened, she said.
Long-term structural change in the ferrous scrap sector with increasing use of electric arc furnaces, favoured increasing volumes of traded scrap, Klemm said.
The strongest growth in electric arc furnace demand was in Asia where Metalcorp had established a market presence through Metal Recyclers, she said.
"Metalcorp expects steady growth in scrap demand and sees profitability increases being derived through more efficient collection systems and networks," Klemm said.
"With a strong balance sheet and preference for minimal debt, Metalcorp is well placed to continue its exceptional growth," Klemm said.
The difficult market provided opportunities to increase market share and growth through acquisition, she said.
Business integration benefits and economies of scale emerging from the group's nationally growing merchandising and recycling networks would boost future earnings.
Metalcorp also had recently seen a substantial re-rating in share price with a further boost on speculation of a further acquisition, Klemm said.
"The stock is trading on sound fundamentals and investment is recommended," Klemm said.
